deep.reconstruction:
Folio [164] contains two short 'Lehrsätze' (theorems). The previous page is crystallography (aragonite, calcite). The column at the right edge, headed 'Ablesung', belongs to the facing page, which is the next folio.

PART 1 – Complex form of the focal property of conjugate semi-diameters.
Claim: Let the ellipse be centred at the origin of the complex plane. Let t, t' be the complex numbers (vectors from the centre) of two conjugate semi-diameters. Let ε be the complex number of a focus, i.e. the vector from the centre to a focus. Then t^2 + t'^2 = ε^2.

Gauss's proof sketch:
(a) Every centred ellipse can be written z(x) = g e^{ix} + h e^{-ix}, with g, h complex and 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π.
(b) Two conjugate semi-diameters are t = z(x) = g e^{ix} + h e^{-ix} and t' = z(x + π/2) = i g e^{ix} − i h e^{-ix]. [Mine: t' is the parameter shifted by a quarter period. It is the derivative dz/dx, i.e. the tangent direction at t, and that is what makes it conjugate to t.]
(c) [Mine, implicit] Squaring and adding:
 t^2 = g^2 e^{2ix} + 2gh + h^2 e^{-2ix},
 t'^2 = −g^2 e^{2ix} + 2gh − h^2 e^{-2ix},
 so t^2 + t'^2 = 4gh, independent of x.
(d) 'Also 4gh = εε'. [Mine, justification] Write g = |g| e^{iα} and h = |h| e^{iβ}.
 - The semi-axes are |g|+|h| and ||g|−|h||. They lie along the directions e^{i(α+β)/2} and i e^{i(α+β)/2}; these are the points where the two rotating vectors are parallel or antiparallel.
 - The focal distance c therefore satisfies c^2 = (|g|+|h|)^2 − (|g|−|h|)^2 = 4|g||h|.
 - The focus lies on the major axis, so ε = ±2√(|g||h|) e^{i(α+β)/2}.
 - Hence ε^2 = 4|g||h| e^{i(α+β)} = 4gh.
Combining (c) and (d) gives t^2 + t'^2 = ε^2. Equivalently, the foci are ±√(t^2 + t'^2).
This is the complex-number version of Apollonius's theorem on conjugate diameters. It holds for any pair of conjugate semi-diameters.

PART 2 – Chord of the sphere from its stereographic projection.
Setup: Let C be the centre of the projection plane and N the projection pole. N lies on the normal erected at C, at height CN equal to the sphere's diameter 2r. Gauss notes this also equals the radius of the projected equator, i.e. projection is onto the tangent plane at the antipode.
Claim: For sphere points Q, Q' with projections P, P',
 chord QQ' = PP' · (CN/PN) · (CN/P'N).
Here CN/PN and CN/P'N are the cosines of the angles that the lines PN and P'N make with the normal CN.
[Mine, justification] Stereographic projection from N is the restriction of an inversion centred at N with power CN^2 = (2r)^2. Any inversion of power k^2 satisfies |XY| = k^2 |X'Y'| / (|NX'| |NY'|). This gives exactly the stated formula.
Gauss then remarks:
 - The formula yields the chord 2r sin(θ/2), a quantity proportional to the sine of half the arc θ.
 - It is 'better' to describe the projection by 'bicomplex' quantities t, t'. The tangent of the half arc is then given by (t' − t)/(1 + t t').
 - Alternatively one could use 'tricomplex' quantities.
[Mine] In modern terms, take the unit sphere projected from a pole onto the equatorial plane. Then tan(θ/2) = |w − z| / |1 + conj(z) w|. For points on one great circle through the poles, t = tan(φ/2) is real and this reduces to the tangent-subtraction formula (t' − t)/(1 + t t'). The word 'bicomplex' presumably refers to some device that absorbs the conjugation.
errors: In the second conjugate semi-diameter, the manuscript appears to write 'gie^{ix} − hie^{ix}'; the exponent of the second term should be −ix. This is a slip of the pen (the machine transcription silently corrects it).
The step 4gh = εε is asserted without proof. It is correct, but the identification of the foci requires the argument supplied in the reconstruction.

The half-arc tangent (t' − t)/(1 + t t') is literally correct only for 'real' parameters, i.e. points on one meridian. For general points in the complex plane the denominator needs a conjugate: |1 + conj(t) t'|. Gauss's 'bicomplex' remark suggests he intended a formalism that takes care of this, but as written it is incomplete.

The phrase 'Normale aequal dem Durchmesser der Kugel' presupposes projection onto the tangent plane at the antipode of N. With the plane through the centre the factor changes. Within his stated convention the formula is consistent.

results.what: For an ellipse with centre 0 and complex conjugate semi-diameters t, t', the foci are ±ε with ε^2 = t^2 + t'^2. Proof via the parametrisation g e^{ix} + h e^{-ix}, giving t^2 + t'^2 = 4gh.
results.modern_name: Complex form of Apollonius' conjugate-diameter theorem; focus formula ε = ±√(t^2 + t'^2) (used e.g. in proofs of Marden/Siebeck theorem on Steiner inellipse)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical in 19th-century complex-number geometry (Siebeck 1864, Laguerre, later Morley); no single firm attribution

results.what: Representation of an ellipse as the sum of two counter-rotating vectors g e^{ix} + h e^{-ix}
results.modern_name: Epicyclic / two-phasor (positive and negative frequency) representation of an ellipse
results.usually_credited_to: Classical; appears in Gauss's own writings and in 19th-century kinematics

results.what: Chord between two sphere points equals the distance of their stereographic images times CN^2/(PN·P'N)
results.modern_name: Stereographic projection as inversion; chordal metric formula
results.usually_credited_to: Inversion viewpoint: W. Thomson / Liouville (1840s); chordal metric on the Riemann sphere standard later (Carathéodory, Ostrowski)

results.what: Tangent of half the spherical distance expressed as (t' − t)/(1 + t t') in projection coordinates; suggestion to use 'bicomplex'/'tricomplex' quantities
results.modern_name: Invariant distance on the sphere under the rotation group SU(2): tan(θ/2) = |z−w|/|1+conj(z)w|
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Möbius/Cayley/Klein treatments of sphere rotations as linear fractional maps (mid/late 19th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: Both results are elementary once stated. The neat complex-number identity t^2 + t'^2 = ε^2 for conjugate semi-diameters and foci is normally met in later 19th-century complex geometry, so finding it around 1809 with a clean proof is a notable unpublished detail. The chord/inversion fact is routine for Gauss, who knew stereographic projection well. The hint at 'bicomplex/tricomplex' quantities for spherical distance ties in with his known private work on space transformations, but it is only a remark.

transcription_corrections: Second semi-diameter: the manuscript appears to read 'gie^{ix} − hie^{ix}' (minus sign missing in the second exponent). The transcription's −ix is the mathematically correct reading.
'Distanz[?]' after the second formula is probably the start of 'Die Distanz…', broken off. 'Also 4gh = εε' is written above it.
Struck words: '[-in der Grösse-]' is correct. The struck word before 'haben' is illegible.

The right-margin column 'Ablesung 0, 90, 90°+θ, 360°−k, x, x+θ, 2x, soll dann d…, muss x, 2x' is the edge of the facing (next) page, a reflection-goniometer protocol. It is not part of this page's content.
'Halbaxen' here means conjugate semi-diameters, not only the principal semi-axes.
